about.title: ABOUT
body: # FLIGHT QUARTERS
HypeTeen Flight Quarters is the Flight Club Intro Academy, a companion to the HypeTeen Flight Academy books. Cadets explore an airfield, meet the crew and work through ground school.
# FOR FAMILIES
Everything stays on this device. Cadets enroll with a made-up call sign and a 4-digit PIN. No real names, emails or photos are asked for.
The first cadet enrolled on a device becomes the FAMILY LEAD, who can reset a forgotten PIN in Settings and post Hangar News.
# HOW TO PLAY
Tap the floor to walk. Tap people and signs to use them. The bar at the bottom jumps between the Lounge, the Hangar, the Viewing Platform and the Runway. FLIGHT BAG opens everything as a list.

aircraft.title: AIRCRAFT GALLERY
body: # KINDS OF AIRCRAFT
Pilots sort aircraft into categories. These are the ones on a pilot certificate:
# AIRPLANE
Fixed wings and an engine. Most student pilots learn in a small airplane like the trainer in our hangar.
# ROTORCRAFT
Spinning blades make the lift. Helicopters are rotorcraft, and so are gyroplanes.
# GLIDER
No engine needed once it’s flying. Gliders ride rising air to stay up.
# LIGHTER-THAN-AIR
Hot-air balloons and airships float because they’re lighter than the air around them.
# POWERED-LIFT
Takes off like a helicopter and flies like an airplane. Tiltrotors are powered-lift.
# POWERED PARACHUTE + WEIGHT-SHIFT
Two kinds of light aircraft. One hangs under a parachute-style wing. The other is steered by shifting weight, like a hang glider with an engine.
# COMING NEXT
Classes inside each category (single-engine, multi-engine, land and sea) arrive with Ground School.

radio.title: TOWER RADIO
body: # THE PHONETIC ALPHABET
Pilots spell with words so letters never get mixed up over a scratchy radio.
A  ALFA  •  B  BRAVO  •  C  CHARLIE  •  D  DELTA
E  ECHO  •  F  FOXTROT  •  G  GOLF  •  H  HOTEL
I  INDIA  •  J  JULIETT  •  K  KILO  •  L  LIMA
M  MIKE  •  N  NOVEMBER  •  O  OSCAR  •  P  PAPA
Q  QUEBEC  •  R  ROMEO  •  S  SIERRA  •  T  TANGO
U  UNIFORM  •  V  VICTOR  •  W  WHISKEY  •  X  X-RAY
Y  YANKEE  •  Z  ZULU
# NUMBERS
Numbers are said one digit at a time, and nine is said NINER.
# RADIO WORDS
ROGER: I heard you.
WILCO: I will comply.
SAY AGAIN: please repeat that.
AFFIRMATIVE: yes.  NEGATIVE: no.

windsock.title: THE WINDSOCK
body: A windsock shows two things at a glance: which way the wind is blowing, and roughly how strong it is.
# DIRECTION
Wind blows into the big open end and out the small end, so the sock points the way the wind is going.
# STRENGTH
A limp sock means calm air. The fatter and straighter it flies, the stronger the wind.
# WHY PILOTS CARE
Airplanes take off and land into the wind. A headwind slows the airplane over the ground, so it needs less runway.
